docs.title: Frontend notices
docs.text:
The browser-component record binds the retained MaterialX 10.1.5 browser assets to exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps. The existing catalogue and third-party product terms remain unchanged.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 34 unused lunr-languages 1.14.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. Nine core vendor assets remain byte-identical. Historical complete outputs remain recovery evidence; omitted helpers are not represented as currently distributed or relicensed.

The main source map retains 211 preferred sources, including 128 exact NPM source matches; the worker map retains 13 sources, including Lunr 2.3.9. The exact clipboard distribution embeds its dependencies; select, good-listener and delegate retain their upstream README MIT link and Zeno Rocha attribution, without invented standalone licence text or dates. CSS maps retain source names without embedded source bodies.

Material Design icons retain the Pictogrammers notice and Apache 2.0 icon terms or specifically stated underlying terms; code is MIT. Font Awesome Free retains Fonticons attribution and CC-BY 4.0 terms. Octicons retains GitHub's MIT notice; Lucide retains ISC and inherited notices. Of 45 observed SVG path tuples, 43 match installed icons exactly. Two optimized CSS tuples have source attribution: Lucide focus/download in the pinned SCSS. This does not assert equivalence of all SVG geometry.

FontLab's shared theme and the existing Adobe Fonts stylesheet remain external HTTPS services (theme.font is false). Their implementation/font bytes are not copied into this payload; reference notices below do not freeze future responses. Build dependencies and local/hosted publication have separate qualification.

docs.title: TypeRig
docs.text:
Tools panel Match Contours

TypeRig is a mighty collection of tools and scripts that extend the FontLab 8 & 7 font editor. TypeRig is developed by Vassil Kateliev. It works on the newest FontLab 8, and should work on FontLab 7 as well. Future versions will focus on FontLab 8.

docs.title: Fix Python in FontLab 8 on macOS 10.13 High Sierra
docs.text:
If you’re running FontLab 8 on macOS 10.13 High Sierra and would like to use Python scripts, you need to run a special fix. This is only needed on macOS 10.13 High Sierra, not any newer macOS systems.

  1. Download fix_fontlab_8_for_macos_10_13.vfpy
  2. Open FontLab 8, choose File > Open, navigate to your Downloads folder and open the downloaded fix_fontlab_8_for_macos_10_13.vfpy file.
  3. You’ll be asked to download and install Python 3.10.5. Follow the instructions and when you have installed Python, restart FontLab.
